provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1962 reads `beatae` where 1862 reads `be&tee`; 1962 reads `solemnia` where 1862 reads `sol6mnia`; 1962 reads `meritis` where 1862 reads `m6ritis`; 1962 reads `precibus.` where 1862 reads `pr6cibus.`; 1962 has `nostrum Iesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.`; 1862 has nothing there; 1862 sets no comma after the opening ut, and one before `et precibus`; 1862 conclusion is the short cue; the 1962 writes it out in full; 1862 layer reads the ae ligature as `ee` twice. Corroboration: 1922 Mame carries 23 November at PDF pp. 875-876; not transcribed.

publication.evidence: The wording is preexisting material of the 1962 typical edition under 17 U.S.C. 103(b), which gives a revised edition no exclusive right in material it did not contribute. The independent registered public-domain witness is the tracked 1862 Pustet text artifact. The position is settled for the repository at src/sources/inventories/missale-romanum-1962-facsimile-rights-v1.toml, which names the seasonal orations as preexisting material and requires exactly this pairing of 103(b) with a public-domain witness.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Praesta, quaesumus, omnipotens Deus: ut, beatae Felicitatis Martyris tuae
solemnia recensentes, meritis ipsius protegamur et precibus. Per Dominum
nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Historical source comm-s-felicitatis-martyris/main/Collect/all/1; same-witness-conclusion-table.
